description: August is Jakarta's clearest international fine-dining benchmark, combining contemporary Indonesian flavour memory with polished global technique and unusually warm hospitality. The intimate SCBD room, chef's counter energy and Asia's 50 Best recognition make it the first booking for affluent diners tracking Indonesia's new gastronomic confidence.
highlights: Asia's 50 Best No. 42 in 2026, Best Restaurant in Indonesia, chef's counter, contemporary Indonesian tasting menu.
sources: Asia's 50 Best Restaurants; August; Tatler Best Indonesia 2026; Best Eats 2026; CNA Luxury

description: Kindling has quickly become one of the defining Jakarta openings of the mid-2020s, set in a characterful Cikini house and built around a personal Indonesian-Chinese narrative filtered through French technique. Its Best Eats 2026 Restaurant of the Year recognition confirms that it has moved beyond promising newcomer status into the city's most serious fine-dining tier.
highlights: Best Eats 2026 Restaurant of the Year, Cikini heritage-house setting, Indonesian-Chinese flavours, French technique.
sources: Best Eats 2026; Tatler Best Indonesia 2026; BIKO Group; CNA Luxury; Manual Jakarta

description: ESA is one of the restaurants most responsible for reframing Jakarta as a contemporary fine-dining destination rather than simply a city of excellent traditional food. Chef Aditya Muskita's cooking is rooted in Indonesian memory and produce but presented with the precision, restraint and narrative structure expected by international tasting-menu diners.
highlights: La Liste New Destination Champion ambassador, modern Jakarta cuisine, SCBD Park address, strong tasting-menu credibility.
sources: CNA Luxury; La Liste; Tatler Best Indonesia 2026; ESA Restaurant; SCMP

description: Namaaz remains Jakarta's most famous avant-garde Indonesian tasting-menu restaurant, known for playful, multi-course reinterpretations of familiar dishes. It is theatrical, personal and deeply local in reference, giving affluent visitors a dinner experience that could not be confused with a generic international hotel restaurant.
highlights: Experimental Indonesian tasting menu, halal fine-dining positioning, theatrical presentation, long-running destination status.
sources: Namaaz Dining; What's New Indonesia; Jakarta Tourism; Tatler Dining; World of Mouth

description: The Crown gives Jakarta a major new luxury-hotel tasting-menu restaurant led by Kirk Westaway, the chef behind two-Michelin-starred JAAN in Singapore. Its Fairmont setting, 22nd-floor polish and modern British lens make it especially relevant for diners who want recognisable international fine dining with a Jakarta address.
highlights: Kirk Westaway project, Fairmont Jakarta, refined tasting menu, high-rise Senayan setting.
sources: Fairmont Jakarta; SCMP; DestinAsian; What's New Indonesia; Tatler Best Indonesia 2026

description: Amuz is Jakarta's classic serious French dining room, long associated with chef Gilles Marx and the city's business-and-occasion crowd. The room feels formal without being stiff, with polished service, a strong wine posture and a repertoire that still matters in a city now dominated by newer chef-driven concepts.
highlights: Long-running French fine-dining address, SCBD business-dinner relevance, chef Gilles Marx, polished wine-led service.
sources: Amuz Gourmet; What's New Indonesia; Tatler Dining; World of Mouth; local concierge recommendations

description: Morimoto Jakarta brings Masaharu Morimoto's global Japanese style to the 63rd floor of The Langham, pairing sushi-bar theatre with skyline drama. It is an obvious affluent-dining choice for guests who want a luxurious Japanese dinner, polished service and a setting that feels emphatically Jakarta rather than anonymous hotel dining.
highlights: Masaharu Morimoto restaurant, 63rd-floor skyline views, sushi and Japanese-Western signatures, luxury Langham setting.
sources: The Langham Jakarta; Morimoto; Manual Jakarta; Time Out; Chope

description: T'ang Court is one of Jakarta's most convincing luxury Cantonese rooms, carrying the lineage of The Langham's Hong Kong original into a dramatic 61st-floor setting. Premium seafood, private-room hospitality and skyline views make it a natural choice for affluent family celebrations, business dinners and high-end Chinese dining.
highlights: Luxury Cantonese dining, 61st-floor Langham setting, live seafood, private rooms, T'ang Court lineage.
sources: The Langham Jakarta; MICHELIN Guide Hotels; Tatler Dining; Chope; local luxury-hotel dining sources

description: OKU is the polished Japanese anchor at Hotel Indonesia Kempinski, known for refined omakase-style menus, sharp service and a minimalist room that works for both business and special-occasion dinners. It remains one of the city's most dependable luxury-hotel Japanese restaurants.
highlights: Refined Japanese dining, omakase menus, Hotel Indonesia Kempinski setting, central Thamrin address.
sources: Hotel Indonesia Kempinski; What's New Indonesia; Chope; local luxury dining guides

description: JinJoo brings a modern Korean multi-course format to South Jakarta, with a more mature, chef-driven feel than the city's many casual Korean restaurants. Its Best Eats 2026 top-ten placement and intimate Kompound setting make it a strong option for diners looking beyond the usual Japanese, French and Indonesian fine-dining routes.
highlights: Best Eats 2026 top ten, modern Korean multi-course format, Kompound address, serious chef-driven alternative.
sources: Best Eats 2026; DestinAsian; TableCheck; Tatler Dining; Manual Jakarta

description: Li Lian gives Park Hyatt Jakarta a glamorous Cantonese restaurant with a chef pedigree suited to high-end dim sum, roast meats, seafood and celebration dinners. The room's elevated hotel setting and Best Eats 2026 Best New Opening signal make it one of the most relevant newer Chinese-dining additions in the city.
highlights: Best Eats 2026 Best New Opening, Park Hyatt Jakarta setting, refined Cantonese cooking, chef Tan Kwang Aik.
sources: Park Hyatt Jakarta; Best Eats 2026; Prestige; Tatler Dining; Chope

description: SU MA is one of Jakarta's most thoughtful small dining rooms, shaped by Chinese-Indonesian, Korean and broader East Asian references rather than luxury-hotel convention. Its chef-driven format, sleek Blok M setting and current critical attention make it a compelling choice for diners who value personality and craft over formality.
highlights: Forward-looking East Asian tasting menu, Blok M setting, Chinese-Indonesian and Korean influences, current critical momentum.
sources: SU MA; The Peak Magazine; NOW! Jakarta; Prestige; Manual Jakarta; CNA Luxury

description: 1945 is Fairmont Jakarta's refined Indonesian dining room, useful for visitors who want archipelago flavours in a polished five-star setting rather than a relaxed local restaurant. The relaunch and contemporary presentation have kept it relevant as a luxury-hotel expression of Indonesian cuisine.
highlights: Five-star hotel Indonesian dining, contemporary presentation, Fairmont Jakarta, polished Senayan room.
sources: Fairmont Jakarta; What's New Indonesia; FoodieS; NOW! Jakarta; Jakarta Post

description: Henshin remains Jakarta's most recognisable high-rise Nikkei destination, occupying the top floors of The Westin with a combination of serious Peruvian-Japanese cooking, cocktails and skyline theatre. It is especially relevant for affluent diners who want a full evening experience rather than a quiet tasting-menu room.
highlights: Nikkei cuisine, top-floor Westin setting, skyline views, cocktail programme, special-occasion energy.
sources: Henshin; The Westin Jakarta; Marriott; What's New Indonesia; Exquisite Taste Magazine

description: Tom's by Tom Aikens is The Langham's European dining room, balancing celebrity-chef pedigree with a clubby SCBD hotel atmosphere. It works well for affluent diners seeking polished produce-led cooking, wine and a more classic international luxury-hotel experience than Jakarta's newer tasting-menu restaurants.
highlights: Tom Aikens concept, Langham Jakarta, classic European cooking, polished hotel atmosphere.
sources: The Langham Jakarta; Tom Aikens; MICHELIN Guide Hotels; What's New Indonesia; Chope

description: Costa is the strongest current upmarket Mediterranean address in the Gunawarman-Senopati corridor, led by chef Ryan Thejasukmana and built around Catalan-inspired land-and-sea cooking. Its Best Eats 2026 second-place result and Tatler inclusion make it much more than a fashionable room: it is now one of Jakarta's essential high-end casual dinner bookings.
highlights: Best Eats 2026 No. 2, Chef of the Year signal, Catalan land-and-sea cooking, warm Gunawarman room.
sources: Best Eats 2026; Costa; BIKO Group; Tatler Best Indonesia 2026; Manual Jakarta; FoodieS

description: Ironplate gives Jakarta a dramatic Franco-Asian steakhouse built around live teppan-style cooking, polished service and a dark, grown-up MD Place room. It passes the instead-of-Michelin test because the evening is structured around craft, premium ingredients and theatre rather than simple steakhouse familiarity.
highlights: Franco-Asian steakhouse on teppan, chef Andri, MD Place 12th floor, premium grill theatre.
sources: MDA Restaurants; Tatler Best Indonesia 2026; What's New Indonesia; Chope; Exquisite Taste Magazine

description: Salira is Union Group's polished Indonesian restaurant, translating archipelago flavours into a confident Senopati room that feels relaxed but still affluent. Its Best Eats 2026 top-five placement gives it strong current relevance among diners who want Indonesian food with a high-end urban sensibility.
highlights: Best Eats 2026 top five, Union Group Indonesian concept, Senopati address, archipelago flavours in an upscale room.
sources: Best Eats 2026; Union Group; FoodieS; Tatler Dining; local dining guides

description: Bistecca is Jakarta's most established Italian-American luxury steakhouse, with Union Group polish, premium beef, martinis and a clubby SCBD address. It is the kind of place a Michelin diner might choose for a business dinner or celebratory night when the brief is comfort, service and atmosphere rather than a tasting menu.
highlights: Premium SCBD steakhouse, Union Group and chef Luca Pezzera, martini bar, New York chophouse energy.
sources: Bistecca; Union Group; 50 Best Discovery; Chope; What's New Indonesia

description: Altitude Grill pairs dry-aged meat, Japanese-influenced grill technique and one of Jakarta's signature skyline settings on the 46th floor of The Plaza. The view is a major part of the experience, but the premium steakhouse format, wine and special-occasion service keep it firmly inside the affluent dinner set.
highlights: 46th-floor skyline view, dry-aged meats, Japanese-influenced grill technique, premium Thamrin steakhouse.
sources: Altitude Jakarta; What's New Indonesia; Chope; Exquisite Taste Magazine; local concierge recommendations

description: Alto is Four Seasons Jakarta's elevated Italian restaurant, pairing a penthouse-style 20th-floor room with handmade pastas, premium seafood, meat and a serious wine programme. It is less destination-tasting-menu than polished luxury comfort, which is exactly why it belongs in Jakarta's high-end casual core.
highlights: Four Seasons Jakarta, 20th-floor setting, Italian cooking, wine-led hotel dining, terrace views.
sources: Four Seasons Jakarta; What's New Indonesia; Chope; OpenTable; local hotel dining guides

description: Solène brings Southern French and Riviera influences to The St. Regis Jakarta, giving the city a new luxury-hotel alternative with sunlight, seafood, Provence and Côte d'Azur references. The mood is more elegant and shareable than formal, but the St. Regis setting and chef-driven Mediterranean menu make it highly relevant to the affluent dining circuit.
highlights: New St. Regis Southern French restaurant, Provence and Riviera inspiration, chef Maxime Sacchetto Foglia, elegant hotel setting.
sources: The St. Regis Jakarta; Marriott; Epicure Asia; FoodieS; What's New Indonesia

description: Semaja is a modern Indonesian restaurant in Menteng that balances national culinary references with a polished Ismaya-style dining room. It gives affluent visitors a contemporary local dinner that is less experimental than August or ESA but still thoughtful, attractive and rooted in Indonesian flavour.
highlights: Modern Indonesian cooking, Menteng address, Chef Glenn Erari, polished Ismaya room, Tatler Best Indonesia signal.
sources: Semaja; Ismaya Group; Tatler Best Indonesia 2026; Jakarta Globe; local dining guides

description: Young is a modern Thai grill in South Jakarta that has earned serious attention for chef Yohans Gozal's contemporary reading of regional Thai flavours. It is relaxed compared with formal fine dining, but the cooking, seasonal structure and Best Eats top-ten signal make it one of the city's strongest high-end casual alternatives.
highlights: Best Eats 2026 top ten, modern Thai grill, chef Yohans Gozal, seasonal menu, warm Dharmawangsa-area room.
sources: Best Eats 2026; Indonesia Travel; Manual Jakarta; Chope; Tatler Best Indonesia 2026

description: Turkuaz is Jakarta's essential upscale Turkish restaurant, founded by chef Sezai Zorlu and still relevant for long, generous dinners built around Ottoman and Anatolian flavours. It adds an important non-Western, non-Japanese luxury-casual option to the list, with a decorative room and a loyal affluent following.
highlights: Chef Sezai Zorlu, Ottoman Turkish cooking, Kebayoran Baru institution, decorative high-end dining room.
sources: Turkuaz Group; Chope; Tripadvisor; What's New Indonesia; local dining guides

description: Tugu Kunstkring Paleis is a heritage dining experience in a former Batavia art-circle building, filled with antiques, period rooms and Indonesian storytelling. The food is less cutting-edge than Jakarta's new tasting-menu restaurants, but the setting, cultural theatre and grown-up hospitality make it a genuine luxury-traveller address.
highlights: Historic Dutch-era building, Tugu collection interiors, Indonesian heritage dishes, atmospheric Menteng setting.
sources: Tugu Hotels; What's New Indonesia; Jakarta Tourism; local heritage dining guides; World of Mouth

description: Plataran Menteng is one of Jakarta's most reliable upscale Indonesian addresses for guests who want heritage atmosphere, private rooms and a broad archipelago menu in a central villa-like setting. It is particularly useful for business entertaining and first-night local dining where service and setting matter as much as spice and flavour.
highlights: Upscale Indonesian restaurant, three-storey Menteng house, private rooms, heritage interiors, business-dinner appeal.
sources: Plataran; Manual Jakarta; What's New Indonesia; local concierge recommendations; Tripadvisor

description: Li Feng is Mandarin Oriental Jakarta's elegant Cantonese restaurant, built for refined seafood, roast meats, dim sum and private-room celebrations. Its collaboration with Chef Fei from Michelin-starred Jiang in Guangzhou and its polished hotel service keep it important even as newer Cantonese rooms have entered the market.
highlights: Mandarin Oriental setting, refined Cantonese cooking, Chef Fei connection, elegant private rooms, Thamrin luxury-hotel address.
sources: Mandarin Oriental Jakarta; Chope; Tripadvisor; NOW! Jakarta; MICHELIN Guide Hotels

description: ERRE & Urrechu brings Basque and Spanish fire cooking to Gran Meliá Jakarta under chef Íñigo Urrechu, giving the city a strong new hotel-restaurant option outside the SCBD axis. The restaurant is generous, polished and atmospheric, especially for diners seeking seafood, grilled meats and Spanish conviviality at luxury-hotel level.
highlights: Basque-Spanish grill, Gran Meliá Jakarta, chef Íñigo Urrechu, new high-end hotel restaurant, fire-led cooking.
sources: Gran Meliá Jakarta; NOW! Jakarta; DestinAsian; What's New Indonesia; Exquisite Taste Magazine

description: The Coach Restaurant is a rare fashion-house dining concept that has become a genuine Jakarta dinner address rather than a showroom accessory. The Grand Indonesia room, New York styling, cocktails and Best Eats 2026 upmarket recognition make it a credible affluent-casual choice for diners who want design, buzz and proper food in the city centre.
highlights: Best Eats 2026 top ten, Coach's first restaurant, Grand Indonesia setting, New York-inspired design, polished social energy.
sources: Best Eats 2026; Grand Indonesia; Manual Jakarta; Chope; Tripadvisor

description: Café Batavia is the obvious informal-local classic for affluent visitors, set in a colonial-era Kota Tua building overlooking Fatahillah Square. It is more about atmosphere, history and a proper sit-down Indonesian-colonial experience than culinary innovation, but that cultural role is exactly why it belongs in the protected local-favorite set.
highlights: Kota Tua landmark, colonial-era building, Fatahillah Square view, classic Jakarta visitor-and-local institution.
sources: Café Batavia; Chope; Jakarta Travel Guide; What's New Indonesia; local heritage guides

description: Lara Djonggrang is a theatrical Menteng institution housed in a Dutch mansion and filled with Indonesian antiques, mythology and royal-Majapahit references. It is included as an informal local favorite because the dinner is culturally memorable, adult and properly seated, even though the main appeal is heritage atmosphere rather than contemporary technique.
highlights: Menteng Dutch mansion, Tugu collection interiors, royal Majapahit inspiration, atmospheric Indonesian dinner.
sources: Tugu Hotels; Lara Djonggrang; Jakarta Tourism; Qraved; local heritage dining guides

description: Angke is a Jakarta Chinese-Hakka institution dating back to 1965, still valued for generous family-style cooking, private gatherings and reliable service. It is relaxed rather than luxurious, but affluent locals continue to use this kind of restaurant for meaningful group dinners where comfort and continuity matter.
highlights: Legendary since 1965, Hakka Chinese cooking, family-style group dinners, Ketapang flagship atmosphere.
sources: Angke Restaurant; Tripadvisor; Restaurant Guru; local Jakarta food guides; Kumparan

description: Beautika is the relaxed Manado classic that sophisticated Jakarta diners often recommend when visitors want spice, cakalang, woku and North Sulawesi flavour in a proper sit-down format. The Hang Lekir location is not formal, but it is culturally specific, adult, full of character and deeply useful for understanding Jakarta's regional Indonesian dining life.
highlights: Manado classic, woku and cakalang dishes, Hang Lekir address, spicy regional Indonesian cooking.
sources: Beautika Manado; Foodierate; Restaurant Guru; local Jakarta food guides; Trip.com

description: Restoran Trio is an old-school Menteng Chinese restaurant whose charm lies in continuity, regulars and dependable Cantonese-style comfort rather than design. It closes the list as a protected local favorite: not a luxury restaurant, but a culturally credible sit-down dinner that well-travelled diners can appreciate on a more relaxed Jakarta night.
highlights: Old-school Menteng Chinese restaurant, Cantonese comfort dishes, local regulars, relaxed proper dinner format.
sources: Qraved; Tripadvisor; CariBisnis; Restaurant Guru; local Jakarta food guides
